input.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,
input.rationale: Clause 4(a) gives AP a for-any-reason exit on 90 days' notice after the one-year Initial Term (within the 60–90 day fallback band), and the only sum payable on such an exit is fees generated during the 90-day termination period, i.e. no more than three months of fees. However, the same sentence lets Kubient terminate for any reason at any time after the Initial Term on 90 days' notice; because the effective date is not tied to the end of the then-current renewal term, Kubient can walk away mid-term, which fails the fallback element that a vendor convenience right exist only at term end. We therefore make the shortest conforming edit: AP's 90-day right is preserved verbatim in substance, and Kubient's for-any-reason termination is effective only at the end of the then-current Term on the same 90 days' notice. We have not pursued the preferred 30-day/pro-rata-refund position (there are no prepaid fees under this auction revenue model) and we do not disturb the mutual no-termination restriction during the 12-month Initial Term, which is not itself a deviation under our playbook.

proposal.summary: Limit Kubient's for-any-reason termination to take effect only at the end of the then-current Term, preserving AP's 90-day exit right.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We keep AP's right to exit for any reason on 90 days' notice, but limit Kubient's for-any-reason termination so it takes effect only at the end of the then-current Term. Our fallback allows a vendor convenience exit only at term end on at least 90 days' notice, not mid-term during an auto-renewed year.
